To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
• The UK government’s Work Capability Assessment (WCA) for disability benefits is not fit for purpose and should be replaced with a new assessment system.
The UK government’s welfare-to-work programme, Work Programme, is failing disabled people.
the disability benefits system in the UK is in crisis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ways in which a ‘crisis’ of working age inactivitiy has been constructed and understood, and the ways in which policy solutions have been developed and implemented.
the social, economic and political dimensions of the ‘crisis’ of disability benefits, as it is currently understood.
the ‘crisis’ of long-term working age inactivity, and in particular with how and why the numbers on disability benefits in the developed world have increased so rapidly since the 1970s.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the UK disability benefit system has been in crisis for a number of decades, and the situation has become increasingly acute in recent times.
there is a ‘crisis’ of long-term disability benefit receipt, and this is a problem for both individuals and society.
the current system is failing to meet the needs of the people it serves and is failing to meet its objectives of reducing poverty and increasing employment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the UK government’s welfare reform agenda is based on a number of assumptions about disability benefits and the people who claim them, assumptions that are not necessarily borne out by the available evidence.
we have found a complex and contested terrain of representation, policy and practice.
the UK is facing a ‘health and work crisis’ (Wadd et al., 1999).
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a need to develop a more nuanced and sophisticated approach to the management and support of health conditions in the workplace.

the crisis in disability benefits cannot be explained by the medical characteristics of the population claiming benefits, but rather by the way in which the benefits system is structured, administered and regulated.
there is no single explanation of why the number of people on disability benefits has risen so dramatically in the UK over the past three decades.
